method: Every row of every listed final-model four-view atlas was actually displayed and visually inspected. The exact two-draw captures are distinct from obsolete single-draw scout images.

review_groups.observations: Actually reviewed every row in all four views. Bent asymmetrical guard retains defined elbow/forearm segments. Rearward weight shift, knee flexion and jaw preparation develop progressively. Shirt, sleeve and trouser contours stay coherent; no new visible arm stretch, skin poke or abrupt pose change.

All rows viewed from four directions. Neck and torso surge forward while hands retain a compact bent guard; jaw closure accompanies the contact pose. Follow-through is visibly different from wind-up. Sleeve contours and trouser seams remain coherent with no new visible skin poke, arm stretch, or disconnected joint.

Every row viewed from front, right, back and left. Recovery gradually restores the asymmetrical guard and bent stance. Hands and shoulders settle without a sudden end-frame jump. Cloth follows the torso and knees; no new visible skin poke, arm-length change or twisting collapse was observed.

All four views inspected at every row. The left arm draws upward and back into a clear bent-elbow wind-up while the opposite arm stays in guard; knees and torso load before the strike. Forearm volume remains coherent, sleeves follow the shoulders, and the neck stays separate from the raised hand. No new visible interpenetration or cloth tear was observed.

Every integer row inspected from four sides, including corrected collar frames30 and44-46. The left hand extends through the contact arc then recovers across the guard while the torso leans and rotates. The collar and underarm maintain their outline; no visible collapse, new slit or skin poke appears. Upper and lower arm segments remain distinct throughout the forward reach.

All four views checked through the true final pose. The left forearm returns to its lower guard with a gradual shoulder and body recovery; sleeves, hem and knees remain visually coherent. Final frame matches the intended shared guard and shows no stale previous pose.

All rows and all four sides viewed. Compact asymmetrical starting guard with a small preparatory knee dip and weight shift. Elbows, wrists and shirt contours retain their shape; no new visible poke-through or joint disconnection.

Every frame row viewed from all four directions. The right elbow rises and retracts into a higher wind-up; the left remains lower. The body dips and the right hand accelerates forward into its longer reach, followed by a downward recovery. Shirt and sleeve silhouettes remain intact through shoulder rotation, and no new visible arm thinning, wrist snap or skin poke appears.

All rows inspected in the four views. The extended right hand lowers, elbow bends back into guard and torso recoil settles gradually. The sleeve maintains a coherent opening and upper-arm volume. The recovery retains connected wrists and stable garment silhouettes with no observed new skin poke or twisting collapse.
True final endpoint viewed from all four sides. Shared guard is restored with coherent elbow bends and clothing silhouette; no stale pose or visible final-frame jump.

Every row in four views inspected. Both hands rise together into a high bent-elbow wind-up as knees and torso load backward. Hands remain distinct and shoulder motion carries the sleeves without a new visible tear or skin poke. The combined posture is visibly different from either single-hand attack.

Every row inspected from four directions. The high two-arm wind-up drives into a pronounced forward torso dip with both hands extending together at frame42. Forearm segments remain readable instead of collapsing into a curve. Hands descend into follow-through without crossing each other or the chest. The collar and underarm cloth preserve their outlines through the deep pose; no new visible poke-through or fabric collapse appears.

All four views inspected through recovery and the true endpoint. Both arms bend and settle back into the asymmetric guard as the torso rises; garment contours remain coherent. No sudden end-frame change, arm-volume collapse, new cloth tear or visible skin poke was observed.

limits: Visual review checks rendered silhouettes, joint continuity and visible skin/clothing behavior at the declared resolution. It is not an exhaustive microscopic visibility guarantee.
Mouth close-ups, live target interaction and dynamic ragdoll behavior have separate recorded reviews.
Numerical mesh and fabric checks include half-frame samples; these body atlases review integer frames.
